target_customer: Women and girls buying, selling or renting formalwear (prom, pageant, quinceanera, wedding), plus small stores and designers as supply
problem: Formalwear is worn once and expensive; buyers struggle to find and afford dresses and sellers had no good resale channel.
business_model: Marketplace take rate (sellers keep about 80% of price); dresses over $300 routed through Queenly's own quality assurance
product_category: Consumer formalwear resale marketplace and search engine (iOS, Android, web)

founders.name: Trisha Bantigue
founders.background_notes: Former pageant competitor; Forbes 30 Under 30 2022 (Art & Style); inspired by her own struggle to find and afford a dress.

founders.name: Kathy Zhou-Patel
education: University of Pennsylvania, BA Computer Science and Environmental Science (2015)
founders.background_notes: Former pageant competitor per press coverage.

exit.reason: Per a secondary summary of a post-mortem by CTO Kathy Zhou-Patel (Feb 3, 2025): strong engagement but low purchase frequency and high acquisition costs; about $200.8K annual revenue against about $273.8K monthly burn in late 2023; seed capital nearly depleted and a Series A unrealistic. The original post was not opened.

competitors.name: Poshmark
competitors.traction_then: large general resale base; TechCrunch says Queenly aimed to beat it on size and skin-tone inclusivity in formalwear

competitors.name: Retail stores and prom shops
competitors.what: Incumbent channel for prom, pageant and quinceanera dresses

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace with image search and a machine-learning search engine tuned for size and skin-tone inclusion; standard engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Supply and buyer liquidity plus pageant partnerships (Miss USA) gave some advantage, but general resale platforms could list formalwear and switching cost was low.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or clearly copied the wedge in the sources found; Queenly itself acquired Mi Padrino, a quinceanera marketplace, in June 2022. The company ended by running out of money, not by incumbent action.

market_need_then: Dresses are worn once and cost hundreds of dollars; pandemic-era event cancellations hit the category yet Queenly reported about $500K in sales during the pandemic and listings grew from 50,000 (Feb 2021) to 60,000 (Jul 2021).

identity.voice_and_tone: Empowering community tone; tagline about women empowering each other one dress at a time

branding.brand_signature: Crown logo plus the Miss USA partnership and 'Tea Talks' Instagram Live series
branding.community_and_virality: Official Miss USA partnership (2021) with a social campaign, contestant promo codes, and Tea Talks Instagram Live series; over 700K downloads reported by 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative name fit to the pageant audience and notable community and partnership assets, but no evidence it solved acquisition costs, which the post-mortem summary names as a problem.

outcome_analysis: Queenly grew quickly after YC Winter 2021, raising a $6.3M seed led by a16z in July 2021 and buying Mi Padrino in 2022. A secondary summary of the CTO's February 2025 post-mortem says the economics never worked: formalwear is bought rarely, acquisition was costly, late-2023 revenue was about $0.2M a year against a burn of about $0.27M a month, and a Series A was out of reach, so the company shut down around late 2024 to early 2025.
notes: Shutdown cause rests on one secondary aggregator that cites a Medium post-mortem and Kingscrowd; neither primary was opened and my search for the Medium post failed, so treat the revenue and burn figures as unverified. The aggregator's funding list sums to about $9.5M and conflicts with its own $7.1M total; I used TechCrunch (seed grown to $6.3M total including the $2.262M April close; $800K pre-seed; total $7.1M). Pre-seed year 2019 comes from the aggregator, TechCrunch gives no date. CB Insights snippet still lists the company as alive; the YC directory says Inactive, which agrees with the shutdown. YC batch W21. Name origin not found.
